name: Geography trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about countries, capitals, rivers, mountains, landmarks, maps. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which pair of countries are the world's only two doubly landlocked states, meaning every one of their neighbours is itself landlocked?
items.explain: Liechtenstein is bordered only by landlocked Austria and Switzerland. Uzbekistan is bordered only by five landlocked Central Asian states.

items.question: Which landlocked country is the only one in Southeast Asia?
items.explain: Laos has no coastline. Cambodia, Brunei and Timor-Leste all border the sea.

source.title: All 44 Landlocked Countries: Full List by Continent

items.question: Which country lost its coastline when Montenegro left their union in 2006?
items.explain: Serbia became landlocked when Montenegro, which held the Adriatic coast, became independent in 2006.

source.title: All 44 Landlocked Countries: Full List by Continent

items.question: Which two South American countries are the only landlocked ones on the continent?
items.explain: Bolivia and Paraguay are the only landlocked countries in the Western Hemisphere. Every other South American country has a coast.

source.title: Landlocked Countries: Full List and Key Facts

items.question: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world by area?
items.explain: Kazakhstan covers about 2.7 million square kilometres, which makes it the largest landlocked country on Earth.

source.title: Landlocked Countries: Complete List of All 44 Nations

items.question: According to UNESCO, roughly what share of the world's unfrozen freshwater reserve is held by Lake Baikal?
items.explain: UNESCO says Lake Baikal contains about 20% of the world's total unfrozen freshwater reserve.

source.title: Lake Baikal - UNESCO World Heritage Centre

items.question: More than 300 rivers and streams feed Lake Baikal, but it drains through only one river. Which one?
items.explain: The Angara is Baikal's only outlet. The Selenga is the lake's biggest inflow, not its outlet.

source.title: How Deep is Lake Baikal? 5 Facts on this Incredible Lake

items.question: What is the local name for the freshwater seal found only in Lake Baikal?
items.explain: The Baikal seal, also called the nerpa, is one of the lake's most famous endemic animals.

items.question: Which of these capital cities does the Danube River flow through?
items.explain: The Danube passes through four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade. Zagreb lies on the Sava, not the Danube.

items.question: The Danube is the second-longest river in Europe. Which river is longer?
items.explain: The Volga in Russia is the longest river in Europe, and the Danube comes second.

items.question: The Danube's headwaters begin where which two streams join in southwestern Germany?
items.explain: The Danube begins at the confluence of the Brigach and Breg streams near Donaueschingen in the Black Forest.

items.question: Which of these countries is one of the ten that the Danube passes through on its way to the Black Sea?
items.explain: Britannica lists the ten Danube countries as Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova and Ukraine.

items.question: What is the capital of Burkina Faso?
items.explain: Ouagadougou is the capital and largest city of Burkina Faso. Bobo-Dioulasso is a major town but not the capital.

items.question: Which president renamed Upper Volta as Burkina Faso in 1984?
items.explain: The country was renamed Burkina Faso on 4 August 1984 under President Thomas Sankara.

source.title: People's Republic of Burkina Faso - African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights

items.question: Which Polish explorer named Australia's Mount Kosciuszko in 1840 after a Polish national hero?
items.explain: Paul Strzelecki named the mountain in 1840 after Tadeusz Kosciuszko.

items.question: Some Seven Summits lists replace Mount Kosciuszko with a much higher peak in Indonesia. Which peak is it?
items.explain: Puncak Jaya (Carstensz Pyramid) is about 4,884 m. It is used in lists that define the continent as Oceania rather than mainland Australia.

source.title: A Climb of Mount Kosciuszko - UIAA

items.question: Which neighbouring peak, only 19 m lower than Kosciuszko, is the second-highest on mainland Australia?
items.explain: Mount Townsend is the second-highest peak of mainland Australia, about 3.7 km north of Kosciuszko. Mount Twynam is third.

items.question: Which two seas does the Strait of Malacca connect?
answers: Bay of Bengal and Timor Sea
Andaman Sea and South China Sea
Gulf of Thailand and Banda Sea
items.correct: Andaman Sea and South China Sea
items.explain: The strait runs between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula. It links the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) with the South China Sea (Pacific Ocean).

items.question: In shipping, which term describes the largest vessel size able to pass through the Strait of Malacca?
items.explain: Malaccamax is the maximum size of ship that can transit the Strait of Malacca. Larger ships must use deeper straits such as Lombok or Makassar.

source.title: Where Is the Strait of Malacca? - WorldAtlas

items.question: Besides being the driest non-polar desert, the Atacama is the largest desert of which type on Earth?
items.explain: The Atacama is the world's largest fog desert, so some of its moisture comes from fog.

source.title: The edge of habitability: Tracking water in the world's driest desert - ASU News

items.question: Which cold ocean current helps suppress rainfall over the Atacama Desert?
items.explain: The cold Humboldt Current chills coastal air and creates a temperature inversion that suppresses rain. The ocean yields only fog.

items.question: Which country has the highest lowest point of any nation, at about 1,400 m above sea level?
items.explain: Lesotho's lowest point, where the Makhaleng meets the Orange (Senqu) River, is 1,400 m. That is the highest lowest point of any country.

items.question: What is the name of Lesotho's highest peak, at 3,482 m?
items.explain: Thabana Ntlenyana is Lesotho's highest point and the highest peak in southern Africa. Mafadi, the highest point in South Africa, is lower.

items.question: The Maloti Mountains of Lesotho are known by what name on the South African side of the border?
items.explain: The Maloti range in Lesotho's highlands is called the Drakensberg in South Africa.

items.question: What was Astana called when it officially became Kazakhstan's capital in December 1997?
items.explain: A decree of 20 October 1997 declared Akmola the capital, effective 10 December 1997. It was renamed Astana in May 1998.

items.question: Which city served as the first capital of the Kazakh republic in 1920, before Kyzylorda took over in 1925?
items.explain: Orenburg, now in Russia, was the first capital in 1920. The capital moved to Kyzylorda in 1925 and later to Alma-Ata in 1929.

items.question: On the banks of which river is Astana situated?
items.explain: Astana lies on the Ishim River, which is called the Esil in Kazakh.

source.title: Astana, a city by many names - IFLA

items.question: What is the name of the Mekong River's stretch within China?
items.explain: The Lancang is the part of the Mekong that flows through China. The Nujiang and Jinsha are different rivers.

items.question: Which of these countries is NOT one of the six that the Mekong River flows through?
items.explain: The Mekong flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam. It does not reach Malaysia.

items.question: At which capital city is the Mekong joined by the Tonle Sap river system?
items.explain: In Cambodia the Mekong is joined by the Tonle Sap at Phnom Penh. The Bassac River then branches off the Mekong's west bank.

items.question: Which salty lake in Djibouti is the lowest point in Africa, at roughly 150 m below sea level?
items.explain: Lake Assal in the Afar Depression is the lowest land in Africa, about 155 m below sea level. Only the Dead Sea, and by some rankings the Sea of Galilee, lie lower.

source.title: List of places on land with elevations below sea level

items.question: Which national capital is the lowest-lying in the world, at about 28 m below sea level?
items.explain: Baku, Azerbaijan, sits in the Caspian Depression at about 28 m below sea level.

source.title: List of places on land with elevations below sea level

items.question: Which site in Death Valley, about 86 m below sea level, is the lowest point in North America?
items.explain: Badwater Basin in Death Valley National Park, California, is the lowest point in North America.

source.title: List of places on land with elevations below sea level

items.question: Which Antarctic glacier hides a canyon whose bedrock lies about 3,500 m below sea level, the lowest known natural point on land?
items.explain: The canyon under Denman Glacier has bedrock at about −3,500 m, which makes it the lowest natural point on land.

source.title: List of places on land with elevations below sea level

items.question: The Dead Sea Depression lies in a valley on the transform boundary between which two tectonic plates?
items.explain: The Dead Sea sits in a deep valley on the transform boundary between the African and Arabian plates. Shear faulting formed the depression.

source.title: Lowest Land Points Below Sea Level Map - Geology.com

items.question: Which mountain in Russia's Caucasus is generally given as the highest point in Europe?
items.explain: Mount Elbrus in Russia, at 5,642 m, is listed as the highest point of Europe. Dykh-Tau is the next highest in the Caucasus.

source.title: List of elevation extremes by region

items.question: Madagascar is the world's fourth-largest island. Which island ranks third?
items.explain: Madagascar ranks fourth, after Greenland, New Guinea and Borneo.

items.question: What is the name of Madagascar's highest peak, in the Tsaratanana Massif?
items.explain: Maromokotro rises to 2,876 m in the northern Tsaratanana Massif and is the island's highest point.

items.question: Around 88 million years ago, Madagascar split from which landmass, leaving its plants and animals to evolve in isolation?
items.explain: Madagascar separated from India about 88 million years ago. Since then its wildlife has evolved in relative isolation.

items.question: Although Madagascar lies about 400 km off Africa, its people are primarily related to those of which region?
items.explain: Britannica notes that Madagascar's population is mainly related to the peoples of Indonesia, more than 3,000 miles to the east, not to African peoples.

items.question: Which city does Bolivia's constitution name as the national capital?
items.explain: The constitution names Sucre as the capital. La Paz is the seat of government, where the executive and legislature sit.

items.question: La Paz became Bolivia's seat of government after which 1898–1899 conflict?
items.explain: Liberals based in La Paz defeated conservatives based in Sucre in the Federal War. La Paz became the seat of government and Sucre kept its constitutional status.

source.title: Why Bolivia Has Two Capitals: Sucre vs La Paz Explained

items.question: Lake Titicaca has more than 25 tributaries but only one outlet. What is it called?
items.explain: The Río Desaguadero is the lake's single outflow and runs south toward Lake Poopó. The Ramis, Ilave and Coata flow into the lake.

source.title: Lake Titicaca - Facts, Map, Activities - Lakepedia

items.question: At roughly what elevation above sea level does Lake Titicaca, the world's highest navigable lake, sit?
items.explain: Lake Titicaca on the Peru–Bolivia border sits at about 3,812 m (12,507 ft) above sea level.

source.title: Lake Titicaca: Altitude, Map & Facts - Explorandes

items.question: Which peak is the highest in the Americas and in the entire Southern Hemisphere?
items.explain: Aconcagua in Argentina is the highest summit of the Andes, South America, the Americas and the Southern Hemisphere.

items.question: Which Greenland mountain, at 3,694 m, is the highest summit of the entire Arctic?
items.explain: Gunnbjørn Fjeld is the highest island summit of the Americas and the highest summit of the Arctic.

items.question: What is the highest mountain in Antarctica?
items.explain: Mount Vinson is the highest point of Antarctica. Erebus is a well-known volcano but is much lower.

source.title: List of elevation extremes by region

items.question: Which of these countries does NOT border Uzbekistan?
items.explain: Uzbekistan borders Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. Iran does not touch it.

source.title: The World's Two Double Landlocked Countries - WorldAtlas

items.question: Almaty grew up around a Russian fort. What was the town called before it became Alma-Ata?
items.explain: Russia built Fort Zailiyskoe in 1854 and renamed it Vernoe. The town around it became Verny, and was renamed Alma-Ata in 1921.

source.title: Kazakhstan's Capitals: Two Cities of History and Modern Business

items.question: What is the Dead Sea's main tributary?
items.explain: The Dead Sea lies in the Jordan Rift Valley, and the Jordan River is its main tributary. The sea has no outlet.
